event_timeline.event: Binance disclosed a security incident affecting approximately $6.3B in virtual assets; withdrawals were suspended while the incident was investigated.

FBI publicly attributed the theft of more than $6B from Binance on or about October 29 to DPRK activity it calls TraderTraitor; FBI said actors were converting assets primarily into ETH and warned of DeFi and instant-swap laundering.
Binance took the Proof-of-Reserves snapshot later used in its recovery update; Binance says ten named assets including XRP, USDC and RLUSD were fully backed at 1:1.

Reuters reported $4.72B net customer outflows since Binance reopened withdrawals, about 3% of platform assets; Binance reported $2.7B in customer inflows since Sunday and said outflows were stabilizing.

Binance said the zero-knowledge proof for the October 31 snapshot was generated and that users can independently verify at least 1:1 backing for BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD and ZEC; Binance reported about 95% of affected assets replenished.

TradRadar XRP perpetual snapshot: $1.2505 mark, $1.92B open interest across seven exchanges, open interest +1.15% over 24h, OI-weighted funding +0.0077% per eight hours, at least $1.32M reported liquidations, long/short account ratio 3.58 and 78.2% long accounts.

TRM Labs traced 233,461,943.1 XRP from five Binance-attributed hot wallets to attacker account rK21t6nGLy4MNDqhvy3pGwcLFy25qgfzMx. This was the first identified chain leg in the incident; the first transfer alone was 185,017,485.5 XRP.
TRM reports Ripple froze 40.5M of the 88.5M RLUSD taken on Ethereum; approximately 48M RLUSD had already been swapped before the freeze.

Bitcoin.com News, citing the XRPL ledger history, reported the 233.46M XRP was redistributed from the original attacker account into six new wallets through nine large payments; Whale Alert independently indexed two 40M transfers within that sequence.
Bitcoin.com News reported none of the six receiving wallets had sent funds onward as of 04:37 UTC. This is a historical observation and has not been revalidated at the later research cutoff.

A Japanese XRP-ledger research source reports ledger 108064685: the six main recipient accounts collectively held approximately 233,460,920 XRP after nine large transfers; a separate seventh test account had received 1,000 XRP; the original attacker account retained 23.69905 XRP. The source reports no outgoing transactions from the six main recipient accounts as of this ledger.
event_timeline.caveat: This is a source-reported ledger snapshot, not a direct node query performed in this run. It does not establish beneficial ownership, exchange deposit, sale or current status after ledger 108064685.

confirmed_or_sourced_claims.claim: The FBI attributed the theft of more than $6B from Binance on or about October 29, 2026 to North Korean malicious cyber activity designated TraderTraitor.
confirmed_or_sourced_claims.caveat: This records the FBI's attribution; it is not a judicial finding.

confirmed_or_sourced_claims.claim: Binance says the October 31 00:00 UTC snapshot covers ten assets, including XRP, USDC and RLUSD, and that those listed assets were 100% backed after replenishment.
confirmed_or_sourced_claims.caveat: The statement does not disclose that XRP itself was stolen or the XRP-specific amount of any loss or replenishment.

confirmed_or_sourced_claims.claim: Binance says the zero-knowledge proof for the October 31 snapshot was generated by November 2 and that users can independently verify their account balances for the ten listed tokens at a minimum 1:1 ratio.
confirmed_or_sourced_claims.caveat: This artifact does not execute the verifier or independently validate any individual account proof.

confirmed_or_sourced_claims.claim: Reuters reported $4.72B net outflows after reopening, approximately 3% of Binance platform assets, and $2.7B customer inflows reported by Binance since Sunday.
confirmed_or_sourced_claims.caveat: The flow figures are reported from company statements and third-party analytics; the article does not provide XRP-specific net flows.

confirmed_or_sourced_claims.claim: Reuters reported Circle had frozen more than $1.1B in USDC linked to the incident as of November 2.
confirmed_or_sourced_claims.caveat: This is a time-specific reported total; it must not be added to earlier Circle freeze figures.

confirmed_or_sourced_claims.claim: TradRadar reported the XRP perpetual market snapshot specified in event_timeline at 15:40 UTC, aggregating seven exchanges.
confirmed_or_sourced_claims.caveat: The aggregator reports a 15-minute delay and partial liquidation visibility; no independent second provider is synchronized to this exact timestamp.

confirmed_or_sourced_claims.claim: Binance describes a Merkle-tree and zk-SNARK process that includes user balances in a liabilities report and allows users to verify inclusion for a specified snapshot.
confirmed_or_sourced_claims.caveat: A point-in-time proof is not continuous solvency assurance, an operational-security audit, or proof that all possible off-platform liabilities are represented.

confirmed_or_sourced_claims.claim: TRM Labs traced 233.46M XRP (233,461,943.1 XRP) from five Binance-attributed XRPL wallets to one attacker account between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC on October 29; TRM valued the XRP tranche at approximately $296M at transfer time.
confirmed_or_sourced_claims.caveat: This is a forensic attribution based on wallet labels and transaction context; Binance has not published a token-by-token root-cause report. The transfer was from Binance-controlled wallets, not proof of a customer XRP loss after Binance's replenishment commitment.

confirmed_or_sourced_claims.claim: XRPLWin published five transaction identifiers and amounts totaling 233,461,943.1 XRP, with the largest transfer accounting for approximately 79% of the total.
confirmed_or_sourced_claims.caveat: XRPLWin is an explorer/analytics provider; transaction hashes are public and independently replayable, but this run did not retrieve raw account_tx data directly from an XRPL node.

confirmed_or_sourced_claims.claim: Bitcoin.com News reported that on November 2 between 03:52 and 04:00 UTC the original attacker account redistributed the 233.46M XRP into six new wallets; Whale Alert separately indexed two 40M XRP transfers in that sequence.
confirmed_or_sourced_claims.caveat: The 04:37 UTC no-outgoing observation is stale and was not revalidated at the later research cutoff. Two 40M alerts are not the full nine-payment redistribution.

confirmed_or_sourced_claims.claim: TRM reports 88.5M RLUSD was taken on Ethereum and Ripple froze 40.5M RLUSD at 22:01 UTC, with approximately 48M already swapped before the freeze.
confirmed_or_sourced_claims.caveat: This is the Ethereum RLUSD tranche; it must not be conflated with separate RLUSD movements on XRPL or Binance's earlier rounded public statement.

confirmed_or_sourced_claims.claim: Native XRP cannot be frozen or reversed by an issuer; XRPL.org states no one can freeze accounts or revert XRP Ledger transactions. Issued tokens may have issuer-controlled restrictions subject to their configuration.
confirmed_or_sourced_claims.caveat: This distinction concerns native XRP versus issued assets and does not imply that exchanges cannot block deposits to their own custodial accounts.

confirmed_or_sourced_claims.claim: A Japanese XRP-ledger research source reports that by ledger 108064685 (approximately 19:55 UTC Nov 2), the six main recipient wallets held a combined approximately 233,460,920 XRP, a separate test wallet had received 1,000 XRP, the original attacker account retained 23.69905 XRP, and the six main recipients had no outgoing transactions as of that ledger.
confirmed_or_sourced_claims.caveat: This is not a live node query by this run and does not establish who controls the receiving wallets or whether funds were later moved, deposited or sold.

xrp_specific_reconciliation.binance_listed_xrp_status: Binance states XRP is one of ten assets fully backed 1:1 in the October 31 00:00 UTC snapshot; the ZK proof was announced complete November 2.
xrp_specific_reconciliation.nov_2_redistribution: Bitcoin.com News and a Japanese XRP-ledger research source report nine large payments from the original attacker account between 03:52 and 04:00 UTC on Nov 2. Six main recipient wallets received approximately 233,460,920 XRP in total; a separate seventh test wallet received 1,000 XRP. The original attacker account reportedly retained 23.69905 XRP.
xrp_specific_reconciliation.nov_2_no_outgoing_status: A Japanese XRP-ledger research source reports no outgoing transactions from the six main recipient wallets as of validated ledger 108064685, approximately 19:55 UTC on Nov 2. This run did not query a live XRPL node after that ledger; do not call it current beyond that cutoff.
xrp_specific_reconciliation.native_xrp_freezeability: Native XRP has no issuer-level freeze or clawback. Recovery depends on tracing, cooperation and blocking deposits at custodial exchanges or other services.
xrp_specific_reconciliation.interpretation: The theft of 233.46M XRP from Binance-attributed wallets is now supported by TRM's forensic report and XRPLWin's published transaction-level table. Binance's later 1:1 PoR statement is separate evidence about the October 31 customer-liability snapshot. It does not disclose the exact XRP replenishment quantity, and it does not establish that customer balances were impaired after Binance's replenishment.

competing_hypotheses.name: Contained exchange-specific confidence shock
competing_hypotheses.claim: Binance's replenishment, 1:1 proof process and relatively limited 3% net outflow may contain the confidence shock without persistent XRP liquidity impairment.
support: Binance reports about 95% of affected assets replenished and 1:1 verification for ten tokens.
Reuters reports outflows of about 3% of platform assets and $2.7B inflows since Sunday.
disconfirming: Further sustained net outflows
Withdrawal restrictions persist or widen
XRP spreads/depth deteriorate materially on Binance relative to peers
Independent evidence contradicts the reserve statement.

competing_hypotheses.name: Venue migration redistributes XRP liquidity
competing_hypotheses.claim: Some Binance users may shift custody or trading to competing venues, redistributing XRP spot depth, perpetual open interest and basis.
support: Reuters reports inflows at OKX, Gate and Bybit after Binance reopened.
disconfirming: Flow attribution is unknown
No XRP-pair-specific venue flows or order-book migration were measured
Net venue inflows may be unrelated to Binance users.

competing_hypotheses.name: System-wide counterparty risk reduces leverage and risk appetite
competing_hypotheses.claim: A major centralized-exchange incident may raise required counterparty premia, encourage self-custody and reduce leveraged crypto exposure, including XRP.
support: FBI attribution and scale of incident
Reuters reports stablecoin market caps fell after the incident and analysts warned of institutional risk reassessment.
disconfirming: Broader market recovery
No persistent reduction in XRP open interest or liquidity
Net exchange flows stabilize and institutional products continue normal subscriptions.

competing_hypotheses.name: Stablecoin issuer intervention reinforces freeze/censorship trade-offs
competing_hypotheses.claim: Circle's ability to freeze more than $1.1B USDC demonstrates operational intervention capacity that can aid recovery but also creates issuer-level counterparty and censorship exposure.
support: FBI requested private-sector blocking of identified laundering addresses.
disconfirming: Freeze actions were narrowly scoped and legally coordinated
No evidence of unrelated or erroneous freezes
Users may value recovery capability more than censorship risk.

competing_hypotheses.name: XRP reserve verification improves confidence without proving XRP incident exposure
competing_hypotheses.claim: The inclusion of XRP in Binance's 1:1 snapshot may reduce uncertainty about current custody backing, but it does not establish that XRP was stolen or that the exchange has no other risks.
support: Binance's October 31 snapshot and November 2 ZK-proof announcement
disconfirming: Independent verifier failure
Material mismatch between onchain reserves and published liabilities
A later snapshot changes XRP backing or excludes XRP.

competing_hypotheses.name: Cross-chain signing-infrastructure compromise rather than XRPL protocol exploit
competing_hypotheses.claim: The XRP transfers were valid signed transactions from Binance-controlled wallets, and TRM reports ordinary signed transfers on multiple non-Ethereum chains; the available evidence points toward compromise of Binance's signing infrastructure rather than an XRPL consensus or payment-engine flaw.
support: TRM reports 233.46M XRP left five Binance wallets through ordinary signed transfers.
TRM reports similarly valid signed transfers across multiple chains and assesses a signing-infrastructure compromise.
XRPLWin reports the transfers were valid ledger payments and not a ledger halt or protocol exploit.
disconfirming: Binance has not published its final root-cause report.
The exact signing-system access path remains unknown.
Independent incident-response evidence could revise the initial mechanism assessment.

competing_hypotheses.name: Native XRP recovery is more constrained than issuer-controlled stablecoin recovery
competing_hypotheses.claim: The stolen native XRP cannot be frozen by Ripple at the asset layer, whereas Ripple froze 40.5M Ethereum RLUSD and Circle froze more than $1.1B USDC linked to the incident; recovery of XRP therefore depends more heavily on tracing and custodial choke points.
support: TRM's XRP and RLUSD tranche accounting.
XRPL protocol documentation on native XRP freeze limitations.
Bitcoin.com report of redistribution into six fresh wallets.
disconfirming: No evidence yet that the six new XRP wallets deposited to an exchange or sold.
Exchange-level deposit screening can still block or flag attempted cash-out.
The attacker may retain the XRP without market impact for an extended period.

provenance_precision_note: Do not infer a publication or retrieval clock time where the source or capture log did not provide one. Dates are retained at date precision; market and Binance snapshot timestamps are retained only where explicitly published. TRM and XRPLWin now support a quantified 233,461,943.1 XRP theft from Binance-attributed wallets; the earlier UNKNOWN_NOT_DISCLOSED field has been corrected. Subsequent six-wallet redistribution is time-stamped only through the reported 04:37 UTC observation and is not represented as current. Latest source-reported recipient status is pinned to ledger 108064685 (approximately 19:55 UTC Nov 2); it is not represented as a live query performed by this run.
